relations.subject: tool:cbqueryreportgen
relations.evidence: This tool is only available in Couchbase Server 8.0 and later.

relations.subject: tool:cbqueryreportgen
relations.evidence: The `cbqueryreportgen` command connects to a Couchbase cluster and generates performance reports based on the Query Service's AWR statistics.

relations.subject: tool:cbqueryreportgen
relations.evidence: It's assumed that you have already specified this as the AWR repository, and created an index on the document key in the configured AWR location.

notable_absence.finding: cbqueryreportgen requires -u/--username and -p/--password to connect to the cluster, but the page never states which RBAC role or privilege the connecting user needs to read the AWR keyspace. The registry's own n1ql:automatic-workload-repository note (from query-awr.json) records that the underlying AWR mechanism is gated by the query_manage_system_catalog privilege - a fact this cli/ page, evidently written by the tool's own engineering owner rather than run through the same review as the n1ql/ reference tree, simply omits. Consistent with this round's authorship-provenance hypothesis: lighter RBAC citation discipline in cli/ than in the rest of the Query Service documentation for the exact same feature.

cross_component_finding: This page corroborates and extends the extraction-layer tool:cbqueryreportgen record first seen on query-awr.json - same tool, described this time from its own dedicated cli/ reference page rather than as an aside on the AWR feature page. The two pages are complementary rather than duplicative: query-awr.json documents the AWR mechanism itself, this page documents the CLI surface for consuming it.
cross_product_finding: query-awr.json's own extraction record notes that 'the Capella record did not mint one [a tool concept] because its link to the tool is broken' - this cli/ page gives no indication cbqueryreportgen exists on Capella at all, and its own install-location table (Linux /opt/couchbase/bin/, Windows Program Files, Mac OS X app bundle) ties it to a filesystem Capella customers don't have direct access to. Consistent with cbqueryreportgen being a self-managed-Server-only tool, though no page states that restriction outright.
